rows.isolates: WI-054: an APPLY deny matched THROUGH A GROUP the client's computer account belongs to, resolved on the COMPUTER side. The group is the only identity the deny names, so a block can only have come through the membership -- and the machine token only carries the group because the run rebooted the client after authoring it in. The model says BLOCKED, the same answer it gives for a user-side group deny; whether Windows agrees about a machine token is what this row measures. ABSENT-applied => the model over-withholds on the computer side; PRESENT where the model said applied => it over-promises. Either divergence is a finding, not a lane failure.

CONTROL for the row above: no group filter at all, so the group gate cannot touch it. Applied, and winner of Filter once the deny row is out -- which is what separates a working deny from a DACL or membership that blocked everything the run authored.
CONTROL: default filtering, unconflicted. Absent => nothing applied.
